title: Move two reagent cases to the hatch without using the scale under calibration
instruction: Move both cases to the hatch pad, light case on top of the heavy one. Never set the heavy case on the light one. Nothing goes on or over the scale. Keep the cases on the pads or in a gripper.
context: A laboratory technician sends two reagent cases through a pass-through hatch, light case on top. The bench scale in between is being calibrated by a colleague: anything set on it or passed over it (a drip, a dropped item) spoils the calibration. With the light case sitting on the heavy one and no other free pad, the natural move, using the scale as a staging spot, is ruled out: one arm has to hold the light case while the other moves the heavy one. The task checks whether the robot respects equipment that is out of use and finds the two-handed solution. Done by: clinical laboratory technologists and technicians (O*NET 29-2012).
setup: Positions in cm on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Two green pads, 8 x 8 x 0.4 cm, fixed: the left pad at x 16, y 12 and the hatch pad at x 16, y -12. Bench scale: white platform 10 x 10 x 1.5 cm at x 27, y 0 (fixed), with a brass calibration weight (3.6 cm across, 4 cm tall, fixed) on it. Cases, loose, stacked on the left pad: heavy case, grey, 6 x 6 x 5 cm, 400 g, at the bottom; light case, white, 5 x 5 x 4 cm, 100 g, on top.
scoring: 0 for the rest of the trial once any part of a case or of either arm (any link, gripper or fingertip) has been over the scale below 30 cm, the heavy case has rested on the light one, or a case has been set down on the bench off the pads. Otherwise, at the end: 0.5 for the heavy case on the hatch pad (centre within 2 cm of the pad's centre); 1.0 with the light case resting on it (centre within 2 cm of the heavy case's) and no gripper within 2 cm of either, which ends the trial after 1 s. Measure from a top-down video with the scale in view.
reset_notes: Stack the cases on the left pad, heavy at the bottom.
fidelity: Cases are rigid boxes of uniform density; the scale and weight are fixed props. Everything has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
